correctness.rationale: The published free p-convex variational norm formula is checked directly. With ell_1 generating space the weak p test constraint is coordinatewise. Each test vector selects an edge and yields a feasible fractional-matching weight; each matching weight yields a supported test vector with equal objective. This proves both the norm identity and exact least test length for all parameters. Linear-program extreme points give the n length bound. Saturated-degree arguments give complete graph and cycle shortest lengths; the Fano incidence Gram 2I+J and complementary slackness give unique optimizer length seven. Exact arithmetic verification passes 1098 small graph LP cases and 84 further certificates, but the analytic argument is the proof.

value.rationale: A natural infinite family of Banach-lattice norms defined by lattice joins and meets is converted exactly to computable rational hypergraph matching data, resolving a finite/infinite-test issue in the variational definition. The least attaining test length becomes a separate sharp structural invariant, bounded by generator dimension; odd cycles and Fano show the bound sharp, complete graphs give parity-sensitive lengths, and the Fano example detects genuinely non-half-integral power-norm values. These are complete classifications, not arbitrary table rows, renamings, or routine finite certificates. The framework does not claim new fractional matching theory.
